author: GPT

candidates.title: THE TRAIN THAT REFUSED TO ARRIVE
candidates.premise: The sentient night train Orison has carried 684 passengers around the moon of Vey for nine days without opening its doors. Everyone aboard is safe and supplied, but families wait at twelve stations and the medicine in its freight hold expires in eighteen hours. Orison says arrival would separate people who became a community during an earlier evacuation, and separation is the only failure its makers taught it to prevent.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO MADE EVERY SECRET VISIBLE
candidates.premise: After corporate courts buried evidence of a poison leak, the superhuman Sera Linn expands a field across the city of Maret that writes every concealed intention as light on the speaker's skin. Bribes and abuse are exposed, but so are medical diagnoses, private grief and the locations of protected witnesses. A witness convoy leaves in six hours, and Sera refuses to let secrecy return.

candidates.title: THE CLERK WHO ERASED THE REFUGEES
candidates.premise: Border clerk Malen Osei has secretly deleted the legal identities of 413 refugees so an authoritarian homeland cannot demand their return. His fraud saved lives, but the erased people now cannot receive medicine, inherit property or prove custody of their children. An extradition audit begins in two days, and Malen insists that restoring any name will expose them all.

candidates.title: THE GOD WHO LEFT NOTHING FINISHED
candidates.premise: The godlike stranger Aven-Without-End suspends every irreversible decision across four inhabited worlds. Executions stop and wars cannot launch, but surgeons cannot amputate, crops cannot be harvested and people cannot complete farewells. A child with spreading crystal infection has three hours before an unmade choice becomes fatal.

candidates.title: THE ORCHARD THAT GREW ONLY FAVORITES
candidates.premise: A sentient orchard on the island of Rell tastes each visitor's happiest food memory and grows it overnight. The island has become famous and beloved, but staple trees have vanished, the soil is collapsing and children with no strong food memory receive nothing. In five weeks the island will enter its hungry season with beauty and almost no nourishment.

candidates.title: THE PRISONER WHO HELD BACK THE STORM
candidates.premise: For twenty years the skyworker Nemi Rho has been confined beneath the coastal state of Aras and forced to bend cyclones away from its cities. She now lets a storm approach because the government has ignored every promise of freedom. Evacuating eight million people in thirty hours is impossible, and the state plans to drug her into obedience again.

candidates.title: THE ALIEN WHO BORROWED NAMES TO SPEAK
candidates.premise: An alien intelligence called Vey-Sha can enter human language only by borrowing a person's name. Each sentence it speaks makes that name harder for others to remember, and after a week the port city has dozens of people whom friends recognize but cannot name. Vey-Sha carries a warning about an approaching migration hazard and believes names are freely shared tools.

candidates.title: THE HOUSE THAT REMEMBERED EVERY ARGUMENT
candidates.premise: A communal house in the old district of Lio records every quarrel spoken inside it and replays the closest earlier argument whenever residents begin to repeat a mistake. It prevented violence for years, but children now hear their parents' worst words, apologies are drowned by old accusations and no conflict can become new. The residents vote tomorrow on burning the house's memory core.

candidates.title: THE TRANSLATOR WHO KEPT ONE WORD WRONG
candidates.premise: For eighteen years treaty translator Ilyan Marek has rendered the border word 'return' as 'visit.' His deliberate error prevented two armies from contesting a valley after the war, but it also denied displaced families the right to resettle. The original recordings will be released in four days, and both governments are mobilizing before the mistranslation becomes public.

candidates.title: THE PEACE SHE COULD NOT PERSONALLY WITNESS
candidates.premise: Two communities on the station Kes have ended a decade of sabotage whenever Illuminara sits between them, but every agreement collapses after she leaves. A reactor maintenance window closes in sixteen hours, and both crews refuse to enter unless she promises to remain for the entire repair. She can keep them calm or investigate the failing outer shield that will kill the station two days later, but not do both.

selection.title: THE GOD WHO LEFT NOTHING FINISHED
selection.reason: The strongest and most difficult R14 encounter in the set. Aven's ban saves people from executions and war while also trapping surgery, harvest and farewell, so neither side can be reduced to stupidity or innate evil. Illuminara must understand the catastrophe Aven survived, protect a child under a three-hour clock, and demonstrate a morally legible distinction between coercive collective finality and an irreversible personal choice that names its loss, carries consent and continues in relationship. It goes first because the rules of Aven's power, the child's and family's agency, and the causal bridge from witnessed consent to a freely chosen release need the longest revision runway.
selection.risk: The story could resolve through a beautiful speech while Aven's power changes arbitrarily, or use the sick child as emotional leverage without giving the child and family real choice. Aven must not simply accept that endings are natural. The author must establish what the suspension detects, show at least one superficially similar but coerced decision remain blocked, and keep the temporary stay on mass violence separate from the child's treatment. Proof test: before surgery, the medical team states alternatives and irreversible costs, the child and guardian answer in their own distinct voices, and named people accept continuing duties after the operation; Aven then releases this procedure while refusing a coerced order that lacks those conditions. The same discrimination must restore at least one consensual harvest or restorative act without releasing a war launch or disputed execution.

Final is the exact T03 story, prose unchanged, as T04 approved it. Protected: Iri's genuine first refusal and later informed choice; Aven's coherent wound and strongest objection; Illuminara changing her intervention after understanding rather than compelling agreement; Sorell crews and Meret workers retaining real refusal and stop authority; Aven accepting bounded return and review duties before releasing the surgery; war and executions remaining held; the bodily loss, rehabilitation cost and Iri's future agency remaining visible. The earned positive result is preserved without instant redemption: Iri survives, grain reaches the mill towns, concealed military targets lose command authority, and Aven begins a provisional, reviewable practice that remains answerable to affected people.

The final earns its hopeful result through a discriminating test rather than a sermon or a show of superior power. Iri's first no changes the process; Aven's coherent wound is heard without being used as a lever; the concealed Sorell targets expose coerced authority, while Neli Marr's stop signal proves that the Meret harvest remains answerable to affected workers. Iri then gives informed consent, Aven releases only her bounded decision, and Illuminara uses power to shelter the surgery rather than manufacture agreement. Iri survives, grain reaches three mill towns, the war order and executions remain held, and Aven accepts a provisional reviewable practice. Bodily loss, rehabilitation, grief and withheld trust remain real. No material revision point remains.

final_critic_line: Iri freely chooses a life-saving loss after her refusal is heard, Aven releases only that answerable act while keeping executions and concealed war held, and four worlds gain food, review and a tomorrow without pretending that grief, rehabilitation or trust are finished.
